svg.title: C24 / APOLLO DUST CLOCK engineering mission profile
svg.desc: C24, APOLLO DUST CLOCK. Original project: The long-period orbit of the dust-producing Wolf-Rayet binary WR 125. Session C: Astronomy & Space Physics. Scientific question: How well can a sparse long-period spectroscopic orbit and infrared dust episodes constrain eccentricity, periastron timing, dust cooling, and formation duration? Testable hypothesis: A joint orbital and dust-response model will predict infrared decline more accurately than exact periastron-triggered bursts and will expose uncertainty caused by wind-line radial velocities.. svg.text: The long-period orbit of the dust-producing Wolf-Rayet binary WR 125
No project observations acquired · specified cases await execution · shared demonstrations are separately labeled
Jointly infer the orbit and episodic dust emission of WR 125 using
spectroscopy and infrared photometry. The 2024 study provides a long-period
spectroscopic baseline; new work should test its assumptions and predict
subsequent evolution rather than retain an outdated unknown-period framing.
Allow dust formation to lag or span periastron, because an infrared maximum
is not automatically the orbital closest approach.

TESTABLE HYPOTHESIS / NOT AN OBSERVED RESULT
A joint orbital and dust-response model will predict infrared decline more
accurately than exact periastron-triggered bursts and will expose
uncertainty caused by wind-line radial velocities.

rather than enforcing equality to periastron.
